context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: WF-02 Step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER) for REQ-217: independently verify ELIXIR-DEV's existing test coverage (written across two implementation passes, already reviewed by SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER) against every one of REQ-217's 7 acceptance criteria in docs/requirements.yaml, add anything genuinely missing, and quote a real mix letflow.check.test run.

result.summary:
Read REQ-217's 7 acceptance_criteria directly from docs/requirements.yaml (awk-extracted, not paraphrased from a handoff), the full requirement prose, the design doc's section 10 rework, lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and api_pipeline.ex in full, and both existing test files (test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs, test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs, 234 + 329 lines) in full. Cross-referenced every AC against the actual test code line-by-line rather than trusting prior handoffs' characterizations.

ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA-TO-TEST MAPPING:

AC1 (global cap forced to 0 -> every /api/v1/* request 503+Retry-After, Plug.Parsers never runs, oversized body still 503 not 413) -> admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC1', 2 tests: normal request rejected before auth/dispatch; oversized body (>2MB Plug.Parsers cap) still 503 not 413. GENUINE.

AC2 (per-tenant cap forced to 0 for one tenant -> that tenant 503, a DIFFERENT tenant same global cap succeeds, both in one test) -> admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC2', 1 test: tenant A's own share exhausted directly against the real singleton, tenant A gets 503, tenant B (untouched) reaches Identity's 404 catch-all in the same test. GENUINE.

AC3 (successfully admitted request completing normally releases both refs exactly once, exhaust cap -> one round trip -> subsequent request succeeds) -> admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC3', 1 test: global_cap==1 (design doc Sec10.1's own re-derived minimum), two sequential real HTTP requests both return 404 not 503 -- only possible if request 1 genuinely released before request 2 was admitted. GENUINE (SECURITY-REVIEWER step-05 already independently mutation-tested this exact test).

AC4 (downstream handler RAISES -> both refs still released, force a raise in a route handler, subsequent request succeeds) -> admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC4 (Mechanism A)', 1 test: GET /users/not-a-uuid raises Ecto.Query.CastError inside the matched route handler, wrapped in Plug.Conn.WrapperError, caught by ApiPipeline's Plug.ErrorHandler; follow-up request with a valid id succeeds (200) -- global_cap==1 leaves zero slack for a leaked ref. GENUINE.

AC5 (503 body matches Response.service_unavailable/2's existing shape exactly, compared against error_test.exs's own expected shape) -> admission_test.exs describe 'AC5', 3 tests: global-gate rejection asserts the SAME fields error_test.exs's assert_problem/5 helper checks for service_unavailable/1 (status==503, title=='Service Unavailable', type ends '/problems/service-unavailable', detail present, trace_id key present) plus retry-after and content-type headers; Retry-After confirmed read fresh from Application.get_env(:letflow,:admission,[])[:retry_after_seconds] (overridden to 7, header observed as '7', no other code change); tenant-gate rejection uses the identical shape with distinct wording, schema name not leaked into detail. GENUINE, both halt-and-respond paths covered.

AC6 (chain order confirmed by reading api_pipeline.ex: global admission first before Plug.Parsers, per-tenant after AuthPipeline before TenantStatus) -> admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'AC6', 1 test: reads the real source file, asserts byte-offset ordering of every named plug() line, including :release_global_admission's position between AuthPipeline and the tenant mount. GENUINE, reads the actual shipped file.

AC7 (mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass, real output quoted) -> see Verification section below.

ADDITIONAL FOCUS AREAS FROM MY OWN BRIEF, ALL CONFIRMED PRESENT:
- Disclosed limitation (AuthPipeline's own DB work covered only by the global gate): stated explicitly in lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex's moduledoc lines 22-27 ('Disclosed limitation') and restated in lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex's own moduledoc (admission-control section) -- not silently omitted, matching the requirement's own explicit instruction.
- Both crash-safety mechanisms have genuinely DEDICATED, non-overlapping tests: Mechanism A (register_before_send/2, non-crashing completion only) -> admission_test.exs describe 'Mechanism A', 1 test (slot held then freed exactly when send_resp/3 runs the callback). Mechanism B (Plug.ErrorHandler + process-dictionary drain, the ONLY reliable channel for a raise inside a pre-dispatch plug where conn.assigns is not visible to handle_errors/2's own pre-pipeline conn parameter) -> admission_test.exs describe 'Mechanism B', 2 tests, the first deliberately passing a BARE pre-pipeline conn (not the conn carrying both admission-ref assigns) to handle_errors/2, proving cleanup succeeds only via the process dictionary -- exactly reproducing the design doc's corrected pre-dispatch-raise trace; the second confirms handle_errors/2 is a safe no-op when nothing is pending. The route-handler-raise case (AC4, where conn.assigns IS reliable via WrapperError) is a third, genuinely distinct path covered separately in admission_pipeline_test.exs. All 3 paths the design doc's corrected trace names are independently exercised.
- Global-release fix (Sec10.1) sufficiency + no-double-consumption proof: admission_pipeline_test.exs describe 'REQ-217 rework', 2 dedicated tests -- global_cap==1 admits one full request end to end (would have needed 2 under the pre-fix bug); and a post-completion probe confirming the global counter is back to fully free (no leak, never more than one unit held at once). SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-05 handoff already independently reproduced the mutation (commenting out plug(:release_global_admission) -> exactly these 4 dependent tests fail, 4/8; reverting restores 8/8) -- not re-run by me since the diff is unchanged since that independent reproduction and re-deriving it a third time would be redundant, not additional coverage.

GAP-CHECK OUTCOME: no gap found. All 7 acceptance criteria have a genuine, non-vacuous test; the disclosed-limitation requirement (stated in the requirement's own prose, not a numbered AC) is satisfied in both plugs' moduledocs. NO NEW TEST CODE WAS ADDED -- coverage was already complete from ELIXIR-DEV's two implementation passes.

Wrote test/specs/REQ-217.md documenting this full mapping and the gap-check outcome, per this project's test-spec convention (matches test/specs/REQ-216.md's established shape).

VERIFICATION (all run by me, foreground, real output, source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh):
1. `mix test test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 7.2 seconds (0.00s async, 7.2s sync)' / 'Result: 20 passed', 0 failures.
2. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -> 'Compiling 184 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app'. Zero warnings, zero errors.
3. `mix letflow.check.test` (full suite, runs the entire mix test suite regardless of args passed since Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.Test.run/1 ignores its arg list by design, plus an isolated :wasm_hang subprocess) -> 'Result: 3094/3096 passed (6/6 properties, 3088/3090 tests), 10 excluded', 2 failed, overall task exit FAILED ('underlying `mix test` run exited 2'). Both failures are in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest ('rust pin (REQ-165)' tests, test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:274 and :289) raising `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` -- this specific execution host genuinely has no `rustc` binary on PATH, confirmed directly (`which rustc` / `rustc --version` both fail 'command not found' even with the asdf shim directory prepended to PATH). This is a pre-existing toolchain-availability gap in this environment, entirely unrelated to REQ-217, its admission plugs, or any file this run touched -- not a regression introduced here. The ISS-0069 target substring ('default values for the optional arguments') occurs ZERO times in the full captured output (direct grep, count=0), confirmed across the entire suite including REQ-217's own new/existing test files -- no dead-default-argument warning class recurrence anywhere.

This is an environment limitation TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and later gates should be aware of when re-running mix letflow.check.test themselves on this same host: it will report FAILED for the same 2 rustc-toolchain reasons regardless of REQ-217's own correctness, which is independently confirmed by the scoped 20/20 pass and the clean warnings-as-errors compile.

issues.description: This execution host has no `rustc` binary on PATH (confirmed directly), causing Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest's 2 'rust pin (REQ-165)' tests to fail with :enoent whenever the full suite is run here, independent of any application code correctness. This makes `mix letflow.check.test`'s overall exit code FAILED on this host even when every other test (3094/3096, including all of REQ-217's own 20 admission tests) passes and no ISS-0069 warning exists. Not caused by, or fixable within, REQ-217's scope -- flagged for whichever host/environment-provisioning concern owns ensuring `rustc` is on PATH for REQ-165's toolchain-check tests to run meaningfully.
